lightsDescription: Logical lights connected to a relay output or a DMX channel.
addLightDescription: Choose the light type and its physical output.
completeLightBeforeTest: Complete the highlighted fields before testing.
lightDefaultsDescription: Apply to every light. Each light can override them in its advanced settings.
behaviorFadeInHint: Smoothly turning on and raising brightness.
behaviorFadeOutHint: Smoothly turning off and lowering brightness.
behaviorMaxLevelHint: The full slider gives this much power.
behaviorRestoreHint: State after a power cut or an update.
lightNotConfigured: Not configured — set its type and wiring
dmxChannelHint: One white LED uses one DMX channel. D24 maps it to its output according to the address configured on the device.
lightSaveError: Could not save the light. The output may already be in use.
removeLightConfirm: Remove the selected light and its configuration?
relayUsedDescription: Selected channels will appear in selection lists.
digitalOutputsDescription: Eight digital outputs on the controller. State changes are applied directly to the board.
digitalInputsDescription: Input level and the most recently detected gesture. Events are detected after debounce.
buttonActionsDescription: Pick a button gesture and what should happen: a light or a relay. Actions run locally on the controller.
actionsFilterTargetEmpty: No button controls this target yet.
noActiveInputs: No active inputs. Enable inputs in the controller settings.
addEventsDescription: Choose one or more gestures for this button.
noAvailableEvents: All events have already been added.
inputEventClickDescription: One short press of the button.
inputEventDoubleClickDescription: Two quick presses of the button.
inputEventTripleClickDescription: Three quick presses of the button.
inputEventLongClickDescription: Hold the button and release it. Skipped when the button has hold actions.
inputEventHoldDescription: Runs as soon as the button is held.
noEventActions: No actions defined — add the first one.
removeEventWithActionsMessage: This event has configured actions. Removing it will also remove all actions assigned to it.
actionTestError: Could not run the action test.
relayProfile16: Waveshare Modbus RTU 16-Ch Relay Module RS485
relayProfile32: Waveshare Modbus RTU 32-Ch Relay Module RS485
relayBusInfo: Bus: RS-485 · Modbus RTU · 9600 8N1. Slave addresses must be unique.
removeDeviceConfirm: Remove the selected device and its configuration?
deviceClassRelayDescription: External relay modules, for example Modbus RTU.
deviceClassLedDimmerDescription: Control brightness and settings for LED lighting.
deviceCatalogDescription: Search the hardware catalog and start configuring a model.
deviceCatalogLoadError: Could not load the device catalog from the controller.
searchDevicesPlaceholder: Search by name, class, or description…
customRelayCatalogDescription: Custom profile using a standard Modbus coil map.
relayNoFreeAddresses: All available Modbus addresses are in use.
autoSaveHint: Changes are saved automatically when you leave a field.
advancedSettingsDescription: Profile mapping overrides. These options are also available for predefined profiles.
firmwareDescription: Upload one firmware file containing the controller code and panel.
logsRestartHint: Oldest entries are overwritten when full. The log clears when the controller restarts.
logsLoadError: Could not load the controller event log.
mapDescription: What controls what: button, gesture, action and target — a light or a relay. Pressing a button lights up its path live.
mapLoadError: Could not load the map data.
mapHint: Click an element to edit it. The power icon in the corner of a light or relay switches it.
systemMemoryValue: {flash} MB Flash · {psram} MB PSRAM · {free} KB free
relaySettingsInvalid: Check the values: name cannot be empty, slave address 1–247, relay count 1–32, coil start 0–65503.
relayChannelsDescription: The CH label is fixed. Channel names are optional.
firmwareLogEmpty: Choose a file to start the update.
firmwareConnectionError: Connection dropped during upload; checking whether the new firmware is running.
firmwareWaiting: Checking the controller connection and firmware version.
firmwareReloading: Reloading the panel from the new firmware.
firmwareRestartTimeout: Could not confirm the new firmware version within 60 s. The update is unconfirmed; check the controller and its version.
passwordDescription: One password protects the panel and the API. Scripts can use it with HTTP Basic.
passwordDefaultWarning: You are using the default password. Set your own.
passwordDialogDescription: Every other logged-in browser will be logged out.
passwordResetHint: Forgot it? Hold the BOOT button on the running controller for 10 s to bring back the default password. Settings stay.
backupDescription: Devices, inputs, lights, actions, zones, presets and the network and MQTT settings in one file.
backupNotABackup: This is not a Whisli configuration backup.
backupConfirmTitle: Load the configuration from the file?
backupConfirmMessage: The current devices, inputs, lights, actions and zones are replaced with the file's. The controller restarts.
backupRestoring: Configuration loaded. Waiting for the controller to come back…
backupRestored: Configuration loaded, the controller is running again.
restartDescription: Restarts the controller, e.g. after a network change or when something stopped responding.
restartConfirmMessage: Buttons and the panel stop working for a few seconds. DMX lights go off unless set to “After restart: as before”.
restartWaiting: Waiting for the controller to come back…
restartFailed: The controller did not answer within 60 s — check power and network.
firmwareNotApplied: The update was not applied: the controller did not restart and still runs firmware {version}. See the system logs (firmware category) for details.
firmwareRestartedOld: The controller restarted but still runs firmware {version}. The update failed; check the system logs for the restart reason.
zonesDescription: Parts of the house, e.g. “Ground floor – living room”. Assign lights and buttons in their settings; the order here applies to lists and the map.
zoneSearch: Search or type a new zone…
zonesEmpty: No zones yet. Add the first one, or create it right on a light or button.
zoneRemoveMessage: Its lights and buttons are left without a zone. The lights, buttons and actions themselves do not change.
presetsDescription: Named whites and colours to set on lights: in the “Brightness and colour” dialog or with a button action. A preset changes only the white or colour — brightness stays and an off light stays off.
presetsColorsDescription: For RGB and RGBW lights; the white channel only applies to RGBW.
presetRemoveMessage: The preset disappears from the list.
presetRemoveUsed: {count} actions use it — they are left without a preset and do nothing until you choose another.
networkDescription: Ethernet, Wi-Fi and the setup access point.
networkLoadError: Could not read the network settings.
networkApFallback: On as a fallback — no other network
networkWifiDescription: The Wi-Fi network the controller joins. It is saved only after a successful connection.
networkSsidPlaceholder: Type it or pick one below
networkWifiTimeout: The controller did not report the result.
networkScanHint: Click a network to fill in its name.
networkWifiForgetMessage: The controller leaves this network and will not join it again. Ethernet and the access point keep working.
networkApDescription: The controller's own network “{ssid}” (address 192.168.4.1) — for setting up without a cable or home Wi-Fi.
networkApFallbackHint: When it is off and the controller has neither Ethernet nor Wi-Fi for a minute, the access point comes back by itself, so the controller can always be reached.
networkApOffMessage: The “Whisli-Setup” network disappears. It comes back by itself if the controller loses Ethernet and Wi-Fi.
networkApOffViaAp: The panel is open through the access point — turning it off ends this connection. Come back via Ethernet or Wi-Fi.
networkMqttDescription: Connection to an MQTT broker, e.g. in Home Assistant: light and button states and control.
networkMqttDiscovery: Announce lights and buttons to Home Assistant (MQTT Discovery)
networkMqttTopicHint: The start of every topic of the controller, e.g. {topic}/light/1/state. Change it when several controllers share one broker.
networkMqttDiscoveryPrefixHint: Where Home Assistant looks for device announcements. Keep “homeassistant” unless you changed it in the MQTT integration.
networkMqttDeviceNameHint: The device name under Settings → Devices. Empty: the controller's name from the panel. A name you set in Home Assistant itself takes precedence.
networkMqttConnectionHint: The controller connects to an MQTT broker — usually the Mosquitto add-on in Home Assistant — to send light states and button gestures and receive commands. Enter the server, port and login, then check them with “Test connection”. The base topic and discovery prefix can usually stay as they are.
homeZonesNone: No zones — add some to group lights
homeZoneOffTitle: Turn off the lights in this zone?
homeZoneOnTitle: Turn on the lights in this zone?
testDescription: Every light and output, used or not — to check the wiring one by one. Click to switch.
testLightsDescription: Click to switch on or off; the sliders open brightness and colour.
testOutputsDescription: Every output, unused ones too (in italics).
testModuleInactive: Module inactive — turn it on in Devices to test it.
chaosDescription: Switches every DMX light (brightness and colours), relay and controller output at random — a load test of the whole installation. Click again to stop and put everything back as it was.
backupWithSecrets: Include network passwords (Wi-Fi, access point, MQTT)
backupPassphraseShort: The backup password needs at least 8 characters.
backupSecretsHint: The passwords and the Wi-Fi network are encrypted (AES-256) with this password — they cannot be read without it. The panel password never goes into the file.
backupNoSecretsHint: Without passwords the backup has the network and MQTT settings but not the Wi-Fi network or any password — after loading, the controller keeps its own.
backupPassphraseRestore: Backup password (the file has encrypted network passwords)
backupPassphraseOptional: Without it everything but the network passwords loads
lightDmxConflict: These DMX channels are already used by “{name}”.
mqttStatusDisabledHint: Turn MQTT on and enter the server to connect to Home Assistant.
mqttTopicsDiscovery: Home Assistant finds the lights and buttons by itself (MQTT Discovery, prefix “{prefix}”). Every used button is an event entity with its last gesture and history, and its gestures are also device triggers for automations.
mqttTopicsNoDiscovery: Discovery is off — add the entities in Home Assistant by hand on these topics.
mqttTopicLightState: light state (JSON: state, brightness, color_temp, color)
mqttTopicLightSet: light control from Home Assistant, same JSON
mqttTopicInput: button gesture: click, doubleClick, tripleClick, longClick, hold
notesDescription: Free text about the installation: hardware, wiring, addresses. Saves by itself and goes into configuration backups — don't put passwords here.
notesPlaceholder: E.g. panel RG1: Modbus relay address 1, DMX D24 channels 1–24…
notesSaveError: Could not save — will retry on the next change
hooksDescription: HTTP requests (GET, POST…) button actions can call: a Home Assistant webhook, Node-RED, another server. Sent in the background — buttons never wait for them.
hooksEmpty: No webhooks yet. Add one, then pick it in a button action with “Call webhook”.
hookRemoveUsed: {count} actions use it — they stop working until you pick another target.
hookHeadersHint: One per line: “Name: value”. Tokens, say — in configuration backups only in the encrypted part.
hookInsecureHint: https:// only — e.g. a home server with its own certificate
